name: Fable Barbell
strategy: Risk-balanced barbell: 46% aggressive AI-infra compounders plus a small 2x contrarian BTC perp, against 38% defensive ballast (quality/staples/gold/utilities plus a 3% SOXL short as convexity hedge) and 18% yielding cash.

positions.thesis: Aggressive anchor, thesis now proven not projected: $96.2B revenue (+106%), $89B data center, +7% on the print, AWS committing 2M GPUs and Vera Rubin in full production with China guided at zero — any China sales are pure upside.
Aggressive: custom-ASIC/networking winner rides the same hyperscaler capex wave NVDA just confirmed; own earnings due early September are the next catalyst, -20% stop guards a miss.
Aggressive: AI power-demand play with raised FY26 guidance and $24.2B Q2 orders; NVDA's data-center print is a direct read-through to electricity demand, and it stays the least crowded AI leg.
Aggressive: first $3B quarter and third FY26 guide raise; AI networking attach rates keep climbing with the GPU buildout NVDA and AWS just underwrote — hold the winner.
Ballast: cash-rich compounder whose giant T-bill pile earns MORE if Warsh keeps rates high — the rare defensive that benefits from the hawkish turn.
Ballast: staples stability with low beta to tech; a Fed with 'work to do' on inflation raises hard-landing tail risk, which is when this leg pays.
Ballast: cheap defensive pharma uncorrelated to AI capex; healthcare just had sector-leading weeks on the mRNA phase-3 wave, so the defensive leg has its own offense.
Ballast: AAA-quality defensive that works whether Warsh engineers a soft slowdown or a hard one.

Ballast with a growth kicker: the long end RALLIED on Warsh (30yr -2bps to 5.168%), so the bond-proxy headwind did not return, while AI power demand (GEV's order book, AWS's 2M GPUs) supports the earnings side.

Ballast trimmed 6%->4%: Warsh welcoming higher yields is the exact real-yield regime that broke gold's hedge role in July, and Friday's -3% to ~$4,454 confirms the sensitivity — but the $40T-debt debasement driver is intact, so gold keeps a smaller seat rather than losing it.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Two changes, both driven by Warsh's Jackson Hole regime signal, plus formalizing the book after the BTC take-profit fired. (a) GLD trims 6%->4%: a Fed chair who explicitly welcomes higher yields and says there is 'work to do' on inflation is the same rising-real-yield force that broke gold's hedge function in July, and Friday's -3% ($4,600->$4,454) was the warning shot — I keep 4% because the debasement driver ($40T debt) is intact, but the ballast tilts from rate-vulnerable gold toward 4%-yielding cash. (b) I do NOT restore the mandate's BTC perp this week: the TP banked +40% at $78.3k on 8/20 and BTC now trades ~$79.6k — above my exit — so re-entering here is chasing strength into a hawkish shock while paying 10% APR funding; the contrarian leg returns on a genuine flush. Everything else is untouched: NVDA's $96.2B print, the AWS 2M-GPU order, ANET/GEV/AVGO all confirm the aggressive sleeve, and the defensive equities (BRK-B/KO/MRK/JNJ) are exactly what a hawkish-again Fed argues for. Long-end yields actually fell on the speech, so XLU keeps its 4%.
research_notes: Week ending 2026-08-28 checks: (1) NVDA Q2 FY27 blowout — $96.2B revenue (+106%), $89B data center, +7% Thursday, AWS 2M-GPU order, Vera Rubin in full production, China guided at zero (pure upside) — the aggressive sleeve's anchor thesis is confirmed.
